segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, X one is the Incenter: the point where the three interior angle bisectors of triangle A B C concur, and the center of its unique inscribed circle.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Because X one is equidistant from sidelines B C, C A, and A B by the inradius r, its trilinear coordinates are simply one, to one, to one, while its barycentric sub-triangle areas scale directly with the side lengths, a, to b, to c. Toggle the central lines, and X one anchors the Nagel line through X two, X eight, and X ten, the Feuerbach line through X five and X eleven, and the Soddy line through X seven.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Under functional relations, X one is its own isogonal conjugate, the isotomic conjugate of X seventy-five, the anticomplement of the Spieker center X ten, and the complement of the Nagel point X eight. Across acute, right, Kepler, and Kimberling reference triangles, X one remains the invariant center of the incircle.
